liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Uncle John's Band** (2 reviews): Uncle John's Band has striking instrumental lines the reviewer hasn't heard in other performances; The whole band's wandering improvisation in Uncle John's Band into Black Peter is called the night's high point [6][9]
- **Green Green Grass of Home** (1 review): The opener is a song narrated by someone already dead, like El Paso [12]
- **Saw Mill** (1 review): Saw Mill is described as enormously fun, with Garcia playing joyful pedal steel [5]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider was released on a bonus CD with the Fillmore West 1969 set [8]
- **High Time** (1 review): High Time also appeared on that bonus CD with the Fillmore West 1969 set [8]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): The tape cuts off after Good Lovin'; music, likely Lovelight, seems to be missing [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Green Green Grass of Home**: rare: 8 archived performances [16]
- **Saw Mill**: rare: 6 archived performances [16]
- **Seasons Of My Heart**: rare: 6 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd70-02-07.sbd.hanno.10527.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 13 songs; 84 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Rated a middling recording and mix; the sound improves as the show goes on [7]
- **gd1970-02-07.sbd.bean.3912.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 70 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: High Time sounds good here, with clear instruments and little hiss, unlike most versions from the period [13]
- **gd1970-02-07.sbd.naked_jaybird.3648.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 70 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- The opening country songs fit the band's admiration for Merle Haggard and George Jones [7]
- Garcia plays pedal steel on the three country standards that open the show [8]
- Garcia plays pedal steel, which the reviewer finds unusual and inspired [9]
- After the accidental acoustic set in New Orleans, Garcia plays pedal steel on the first three tracks [12]
- One long set with a break, following bluesman Taj Mahal [14]
- The country trio and China Cat through High Time are strong, but the remainder of the show is mostly uninspired [11]
- May be the best night overall of the run for country fans; the next night has bigger highlights but is less consistent [14]
- Green Green Grass of Home was played eight times in 1969 before this show [14]
- The tape runs about half an hour shorter than the complete tapes of the 6th and 8th [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-02-07.sbd.hanno.10527.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by H.B. and Uli Teute; source: Soundboard patched by Audience [1]. Also: Hanno and Uli assembled this composite from the surviving tapes of the show; Source tape came from Uli Teute; this is a new EAC extraction of Hanno's source discs; Patched sections include the start of Green Green Grass, all of Hard To Handle, and the start of Cold Rain & Snow [1][15]
- **gd1970-02-07.sbd.bean.3912.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Don Bean; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD [2]
- **gd1970-02-07.sbd.naked_jaybird.3648.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by EAC>SHN by; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD [3]
